title: Vendor onboarding — contract scan guide
content:
Purpose / quick use
- One-page checklist for first-pass scans when a new vendor asks to onboard or when renewing contracts.
- Goal: triage risk quickly, call in SRE/product/security/legal as needed. Save time on low-risk baseline deals.

Quick triage rubric (FIRST PASS — 10 minutes)
- High risk (must escalate to Legal + Security):
  - Any clause that grants the vendor rights to use Customer Data for training models or benchmarking.
  - Unlimited liability for data breaches or no meaningful cap.
  - Broad audit/subpoena language without controls or notice.
  - Foreign data export obligations that conflict with customer residency reqs.
  - Broad IP assignment from outputs of the service back to vendor.

- Medium risk (escalate to Legal review):
  - Subprocessor lists not locked / unilateral change right.
  - Vague incident notification timelines (>72 hours).
  - SLA credits that are not commensurate with business impact or no remedy for repeated failures.
  - Data retention/return/destruction language that doesn't cover caches/archives.

- Low risk (product/SI can handle with checklist edits):
  - Standard indemnities capped at reasonable multiple of fees.
  - Reasonable data classification definitions (PII, aggregated) that match our expectations.

Clauses to scan with sample redline/snippet preference (first-pass language suggestions)
- Data use / training
  - Vendor SHOULD NOT use Customer Data to train models or derive improvements to its models, services or products unless expressly agreed in writing.
- Subprocessors
  - Vendor will provide a current list of subprocessors and obtain Customer’s prior written consent for any new subprocessor that will process Customer Data classified as Confidential or PII.
- Data residency / export
  - Customer Data will be stored and processed in the region(s) specified in Schedule A. Any transfer outside these regions requires prior written consent and adequate safeguards.
- Incident notification
  - Vendor will notify Customer within 24 hours of becoming aware of a data security incident affecting Customer Data and provide regular updates until remediation.
- Audit rights
  - Customer may, no more than once per 12 months, conduct an audit or review (on-site or remote) of Vendor’s controls relevant to Customer Data with reasonable prior notice.
- Termination / transition assistance
  - Upon termination, Vendor will provide export of Customer Data in a common machine-readable format and reasonable transition support for 60 days, at no additional charge.

Negotiation talking points (short scripts)
- If vendor resists data-use restriction: "We’re fine with analytics for performance/ops, but cannot allow use for model training — our customers require strict separation"
- If vendor asks for higher liability cap: "We can explore a higher cap tied to the contract value for catastrophic failures but need contractual clarity on triggers and exclusions."
- For subprocessors: "Automated notifications + 30-day objection window gives us acceptable control without blocking operations."

Operational flags / red lights to watch for
- Vendor is a startup that trains models on customer data (raise immediately).
- Vendor insists on ISO-only audits but refuses contractual audit rights.
- Contract tries to waive confidentiality for aggregated/derived outputs.

Notes to self / TODOs
- Create a short Confluence macro with these snippets so PMs can paste during vendor discovery.
- Ask security to pre-vet top-10 vendor cloud regions list for residency mapping (ticket created: JIRA-RDW-1342).
- Add example language for escrow/exit for data held on tape / offline archives.

Contextual links / slack threads
- Slack: #vendor-onboarding thread (see threads from Nov 2025: onboarding-salesforce-procurement)
- Confluence vendor page (linked above) — canonical intake form.

Open questions / unresolved
- How to handle telemetry/usage logs that include hashed identifiers — treat as PII? Security opinion needed.
- When to accept SOC2 report in lieu of contractual audit right? set threshold?

Bottom line: Aim to defuse low-risk deals with clear, short redlines. Escalate early for anything that touches model training, residency, or broad IP/indemnity exposure.

Recent edits log (notes for version history)
- 2025-11-02 initial draft (DP)
- 2026-01-12: added 24-hour incident preferred timeline (Maya)
- 2026-02-20: tightened subprocessor consent language and added JIRA link (Sophie)
